title: FRT presentation of the $q$-Onsager comodule algebra and refined $q$-characters
summary: We introduce a concept of counital comodule algebra $(B,δ_B,ε_B)$ over a Hopf ${\mathbb K}$-algebra $H$, where $δ_B: B\rightarrow B \otimes H$ and $ε_B: B\rightarrow {\mathbb K}$ are coaction and counit homomorphisms, respectively. This structure gives a canonical (counital) comodule algebra map $ι_B: B \rightarrow H$. In this paper, we study in details the case $B=O_q$, and $H$ is the quantum loop algebra ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$ for ${\mathbb K}={\mathbb C}$. Here, $O_q$ is the $q$-Onsager algebra with four presentations: (i) the $q$-Dolan-Grady type; (ii) the alternating type; (iii) the root vectors type; (iv) the Drinfeld type. For $(O_q,δ_{O_q},ε_{O_q})$, in fact a 3-parameter family of counital comodule algebras, we establish a Faddeev-Reshetikhin-Takhtajan (FRT) type presentation, which is written in terms of a K-operator satisfying a reflection algebra relation. The coaction $δ_{O_q}$ (resp. $ι_{O_q}$) sends the K-operator to a `dressed' K-operator (resp. K-matrix) using Ding-Frenkel type L-operators of ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$; the counit $ε_{O_q}$ sends the K-operator to the most general (non-diagonal) solution of the reflection equation. The FRT presentation allows to compute the image via $δ_{O_q}$ and $ι_{O_q}$ of the generating functions of $O_q$ for each presentation (ii)-(iv). Moreover, the images of Lu-Wang's generating functions of $O_q$ in the so-called Drinfeld second realization ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$ are obtained, as well as their images via the (ordinary) coproduct of ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$, which enhance two theorems by Przeździecki. Finally, we apply our FRT presentation to the construction of new type $q$-characters for ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$, in imaginary root vectors of $O_q$, refining those of Frenkel-Reshetikhin, and we explain representation-theoretic meaning of such refining.

title: Functorial Homological Mirror Symmetry for Acyclic Cluster Varieties
summary: We introduce the formalism of cluster models, a class of log Calabi-Yau varieties obtained from smooth quasi-affine toric varieties by iterated affine blowups along non-toric codimension 2 centers determined by a really full rank quiver. Cluster models include the truncated cluster varieties of Gross, Hacking, and Keel with respect to really full rank quivers, all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties, and all open toric subvarieties of $\mathbb{C}^n\times(\mathbb{C}^*)^m$. We then construct mirrors to cluster models via iterated Weinstein handle attachments to toric mirrors, so that the corresponding skeleta acquire compact pieces, and we prove homological mirror symmetry for all cluster models, compatibly with freezing, deleting, and contracting vertices of the quiver. This extends toric mirror symmetry and its naturalities beyond the cotangent bundle. In particular, we obtain homological mirror symmetry for all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties. We develop this package with a view towards conjectures of Marsh, Rietsch, and Williams about mirror symmetry for Grassmannians and closed positroid varieties. Motivated by these, we also conjecture that open positroid varieties are self-mirror. Assuming a natural ansatz, we prove this for a class of positroid varieties that includes nontrivial cells in every Grassmannian and all cells in finite-type Grassmannians. Towards this end we introduce a new combinatorial input, the notion of weak $k$-booleanness for permutations and braids.

title: A relative trace formula for the orthogonal Gan-Gross-Prasad model and the proof of its fundamental lemma
summary: In this paper, we propose a comparison of relative trace formulas to study the Gan--Gross--Prasad conjecture. We unfold the relative trace formulas, match their regular orbits, and formulate the corresponding fundamental lemma and smooth transfer conjecture. Finally, we prove the fundamental lemma for the unit element of the Hecke algebra.

title: Classification of quasi-lisse simple affine vertex algebras
summary: We classify all noncritical levels $k$ for which the simple affine vertex algebra $L_k(\mathfrak{g})$ is quasi-lisse, for every finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$. We prove that Fiebig's equivalence between the corresponding noncritical blocks of category $\mathcal{O}$ identifies the relevant parabolic Wakimoto modules and the homomorphisms from the corresponding universal affine vertex algebras. Combining this compatibility with a characterization of semisimple points in associated varieties, we establish that for coprime positive integers $p,q$, $L_{-h^\vee+p/q}(\mathfrak{g})$ is quasi-lisse if and only if $L_{-h^\vee+p/\gcd(q,r)}(\mathfrak{g})$ is quasi-lisse, where $r$ is the lacing number of $\mathfrak{g}$. The classification at the resulting levels is obtained using Drinfeld--Sokolov reduction, singular vectors and relations in the reductions of the maximal ideals of $V^k(\mathfrak{g})$. We also determine the associated varieties at the quasi-lisse levels for all $\mathfrak{g}$ of rank at most six and for $E_7$ and $E_8$.

title: Counter-examples to Conjectures on NCCRs via a Reductive McKay Correspondence
summary: We disprove three conjectures appearing in Van den Bergh's plenary ICM survey, posed by De Deyn and Van den Bergh, which concern the interplay between non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) and the stringy Euler characteristic. Our counter-examples are applications of a new McKay correspondence for reductive groups that we prove in this paper, extending the classical McKay correspondence for finite groups. We obtain explicit formulas for the stringy $E$-functions of reductive quotients in terms of the Weyl group action and stringy $E$-functions of toric varieties; we also obtain an equivalent formula expressed as an integral of the age function over Weyl-fixed loci of a compact real torus. For symmetric representations, our expressions are related to arithmetic Tutte polynomials, yielding combinatorial formulas for the stringy Euler characteristic.

title: On the Cohomological Amplitude of the Locally Analytic Jacquet--Langlands Functor
summary: We prove a local cohomological bound $RΓ_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)\in D^{[0,\dim X]}$ for a pro-étale sheaf with a derived $p$-complete integral lattice whose modulo $p^m$ reductions are filtered colimits of finite local systems on an affinoid topologically of finite type over $C$. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, with $n\geq2$ and $F/\mathbb Q_p$ finite, we apply these local bounds to variants of Scholze's Jacquet--Langlands functor $\mathrm{JL}_\mathscr{B}(Π):= RΓ_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(\mathbb{P}^{n-1}_C,\mathcal{F}_Π\otimes^{L, \square}_{\mathbb{Q}_p}\mathscr{B})$ for $\mathscr{B}\in\{\mathbb{Q}_p, \widehat{\mathscr{O}}, \mathbb{B}_J\}$ and Banach or compact-type LB representations $Π$ of $G$, obtaining $\mathrm{JL}_{\mathscr{B}}(Π)\in D^{[0,2(n-1)]}$ for each choice of $\mathscr{B}$. We also prove that for arbitrary continuous principal series $I(η)=(\mathrm{Ind}_B^Gη)^{\mathrm{cont}}$, we have $\mathrm{JL}(\mathrm{Ind}_B^Gη)\in D^{[0, n]}$, while $\mathrm{JL}_{\widehat{\mathscr{O}}}(I(η)),\mathrm{JL}_{\mathbb{B}_J}(I(η))\in D^{[0, n-1]}$.

title: The finite projective classification of complex spinors via momentum maps
summary: We describe the projective orbits of complex spinors from the point of view of the momentum map. We treat the irreducible spin modules in odd dimensions 1,3,5,7,9,11 and the half-spin modules in even dimensions 2,4,6,8,10,12,14, which are the only cases with finitely many orbits. In the Clifford--Fock model, we construct representatives as sums of pure basis spinors, and the coefficients are chosen so that the representative is a critical point of the squared norm of the momentum map. The resulting momentum values in a fixed Weyl chamber distinguish the orbits. Completeness follows from Vinberg's theory of graded Lie algebras and stabilizer actions, independently of the classical spinor classifications. We recover the classical counts of 1,1,1,2,3,5 orbits in the odd cases and 1,1,1,2,2,4,9 in the even cases, and compute the projective dimension of every orbit. In dimension fourteen we also determine the closure order of the orbits, using the fact that the minimum of the squared momentum norm increases strictly under degeneration.

title: Global-dimension spectra of gentle algebras
summary:
We classify the connected finite-dimensional gentle algebras of finite global dimension whose global-dimension spectra under derived equivalence are not intervals of integers. These are precisely the algebras with AAG invariant $[(2,4g)]$, where $g\geq2$, whose canonical line field is induced by a nowhere-vanishing vector field. Their spectrum is $\{2g,2g+2,\ldots,4g\}$. For each $g\geq2$, there are exactly two such derived-equivalence classes, distinguished by their Arf invariant.
  The geometric foundation is a realisation theorem for prescribed polygon weights in arbitrary genus. For an AAG invariant $[(m_i,n_i)]_{i=1}^b$ arising from such an algebra, the global dimensions attained in its AAG fibre form the integer interval $[\max_i\lceil n_i/m_i\rceil,\max_i n_i]$. By controlling the complete line-field invariant through local ribbon-graph constructions, we determine the spectrum in every derived-equivalence class.

title: From Frobenius seeds to self-orthogonal modules over symmetric algebras
summary: We construct finite-dimensional symmetric algebras admitting nonprojective self-orthogonal modules from Frobenius algebras equipped with a module satisfying explicit stable and homological conditions. The resulting modules have complexity three, and their stable endomorphism algebras are isomorphic to the algebra of dual numbers over the ground field. The construction combines a variable input with a fixed auxiliary factor carrying the required twisting, and preserves the input through specified quotient and corner constructions. The proof combines derived induction, an obstruction to perfect factorization, and a cone construction over a Gorenstein triangular matrix algebra. For a symmetric algebra and a self-orthogonal generator, we describe the derived category of the opposite endomorphism algebra through a recollement with a two-term $2$-symmetric dg algebra. For our counterexamples, it is formal and quasi-isomorphic to an explicit four-dimensional dg algebra. Applications to cyclic coverings of a quantum exterior algebra yield connected examples with explicitly determined numbers of simple modules. The construction works over every field containing an element of infinite multiplicative order.

title: Invariant operations on vector fields on the line are Lie polynomials
comment: 21 pages, this supersedes the preprint https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08538 of two of the authors
summary: We prove that all $W_1$-equivariant multilinear operations on the Witt Lie algebra $W_1$ are Lie polynomials. We study this question in terms of Wronskian Lie brackets and Novikov products, which are abstractions of the Lie bracket $[a,b]:=ab'-ba'$ and the nonassociative product $a\circ b=ab'$ one can define on a commutative differential algebra. In terms of these notions, our main result asserts that the operad of Wronskian Lie algebras is isomorphic to the operad of equivariant multilinear operations on~$W_1$; we also prove a parallel result for the operad of Novikov algebras, characterizing it as the operad of affine equivariant multilinear operations on $W_1$. Two immediate consequences of our work are a characterization of Lie polynomials in free Novikov algebras and a computation of the degree zero homology of the operadic twisting of the Novikov operad. Finally, while it is known that over a field of zero characteristic, a Novikov algebra embeds into its differential envelope, we show that the same is not necessarily true for Wronskian Lie algebras.

title: Presentations of inverse Artin monoids of type $D_n$ via cluster mutations
summary: Let $D_n^\varepsilon$ denote the Dynkin diagram of type $D_{n+1}$ with the endpoint $\varepsilon$ of its long branch frozen, and let $\mathcal{M}(D_n^\varepsilon)$ be the mutation class of any orientation of this diagram under mutations at mutable vertices. For each $Γ\in\mathcal{M}(D_n^\varepsilon)$, we define an inverse monoid $M_Γ$ by generators and relations determined by $Γ$. We prove that $M_Γ\cong M_{μ_k(Γ)}$ for every mutable vertex $k$. Consequently, every quiver in this mutation class yields a presentation of the inverse Artin monoid of type $D_n$. Our argument establishes mutation invariance for the presentations of inverse Artin monoids of both types $A_n^\varepsilon$ and $D_n^\varepsilon$.

title: Frobenius and ozone automorphism groups of root of unity quantum cluster algebras
summary: Many important families of algebras $R$ in the areas of quantum groups, quantum topology and noncommutative algebra are root of unity quantum algebras, equipped with Frobenius centers $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R) \subseteq Z(R)$ and quantum Frobenius maps ${\mathrm{Fr}} : R_{\mathrm{class}} \stackrel{\cong}{\longrightarrow} Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$. We explicitly classify the Frobenius automorphism groups ${\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R))$ and the ozone groups ${\mathrm{Oz}}(R):= {\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z(R))$, and prove that all endomorphisms of $R$ fixing its Frobenius center $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$ are automorphisms for all algebras $R$ that come from partial root of unity quantum cluster and upper quantum cluster algebras (which have been proved to encompass a vast majority of known quantum algebras). We prove three main theorems that give the above classification results from three different standpoints. As applications, we classify the Frobenius and ozone automorphism groups of all quantum function algebras of simple algebraic groups $G$ not of type $F_4$ or $E_8$ and all quantum unipotent cells at roots of unity for arbitrary symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebras.

title: The cohomology of finite simple groups is unbounded
summary: In every fixed positive degree, we show that the cohomology of finite simple groups, algebraic groups and quantum groups, with coefficients in simple modules, can have arbitrarily large dimension. In particular, we disprove Guralnick's conjecture.

title: On sinks and mirrors
summary:
Given a full rank sink recurrent cluster $\mathcal{A}$ variety, we prove that its wrapped Fukaya category is equivalent to the category of coherent sheaves on a stacky elaboration of the dual Fock-Goncharov cluster $\mathcal{X}$ variety.
  In particular, braid varieties for a semisimple group are mirror to the braid varieties for the Langlands dual group. Another example: for compact surfaces with no interior marked points, a least one marked point on each boundary component, and at least two marked points in total, the Fock-Goncharov moduli for SL(2) and PGL(2) are homologically mirror. The results were obtained in communion with ChatGPT Astra.

title: Representations of the Weyl algebra modulo $p^2$
comment: Preliminary version, 8 pages, all comments welcome
summary: Let $\mathbf{k}$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Let $R=W_2(\mathbf{k})$ be the ring of Witt vectors of length $2$. In this note, we are concerned with the study of representations of the first Weyl algebra that are finite-rank free $R$-modules ($R$-lattices). Our main result shows that given an $R[x]$-lattice $V$, it admits a left module structure over the Weyl algebra (equivalently, an $R$-linear connection) if and only if all of its indecomposable summands have the form $R[x]\otimes_{R[x^p]}N$, where $N$ is an indecomposable $R[x^p]$-lattice of rank divisible by $p$. We also classify, up to isomorphism, all lattices over the $p$-Weyl algebra (defined by $[y,x]=p$) for which the action of $x$ modulo $p$ is regular nilpotent.

title: Dlab--Ringel standardization in algebraic triangulated categories
summary: We introduce the notion of derived standardly stratified algebras as a connective dg analogue of standardly stratified algebras. To this end, we extend the Dlab--Ringel standardization method to algebraic triangulated categories and show that every basic proper derived standardly stratified algebra arises from this extended method. We establish Ringel duality for derived standardly stratified algebras using silting objects. More precisely, the Ringel dual is again derived standardly stratified, and the corresponding perfect derived categories are related by mutually quasi-inverse contravariant triangle equivalences. We also show that, over an algebraically closed field, a proper derived standardly stratified algebra is smooth if and only if its derived standard modules are exceptional. Finally, we prove that dg algebras given by finite acyclic graded quivers with arrows of non-positive degrees and homogeneous relations are derived standardly stratified with respect to every total order on the vertices.

title: Sections of the Kottwitz homomorphism and affine pinnings
summary: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group split over $\mathbb{Z}$. The Kottwitz homomorphism identifies the group of connected components of the loop group of $G$ with the group $Ω$ of length zero elements of the extended affine Weyl group. We show that this homomorphism always has a homomorphic section, and that the section can be chosen inside the normalizer of $T$ in $G(\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}])$. We then ask whether the section can be chosen to preserve an affine pinning. This is possible if no simple factor of $G$ is of type $B_{2m}$ or $C_{2m}$. It is impossible for $(SL_2\times Sp_{2n})/μ_2$ and $(SL_2\times Spin_{2n+1})/μ_2$ when $n$ is even. We show that the obstructions for $G$ and for its Langlands dual group are dual to each other, and we compute them by a lattice computation with a Coxeter element. As an application, we show that the component group of the centralizer of any semisimple element lifts to the centralizer. Under the same condition on the simple factors, the lift can be chosen to preserve a pinning of the neutral component.

title: Finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices
summary: Motivated by the problem of Gragg and Kung on characterizing finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices, we investigate how the consistency of the subgroup lattice $L(G)$ constrains the structure of the underlying finite group $G$. To this end, we first establish several equivalent characterizations of consistency for lattices of finite length in terms of operation-preserving subposets and forbidden sublattices. More interestingly, for complete atomistic lattices of finite length, we introduce the consistency exchange property (CEP) for the canonical closure operator and show that consistency is equivalent to CEP, and that CEP is strictly weaker than the Steinitz-Mac Lane exchange property. We then apply this framework to semidirect products $G=V\rtimes_α C_m$, where $V$ is an elementary abelian $p$-group, $m$ is square-free and $p\nmid m$. Writing $d=o(α)$ and letting $C_α=\langleα\rangle$, we prove that $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $d=1$, or $d$ is prime and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pC_α$-module. For prime $d$, this latter condition is equivalent both to the irreducibility of the minimal polynomial of $α$ over $\mathbb F_p$ and to $\mathbb F_p[α]$ being a field. More generally, we verify that if $G=V\rtimes_θH$ where $H$ acts faithfully on $V$ and $p\nmid |H|$, then $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $H$ is trivial, or $H$ is cyclic of prime order and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pH$-module. We thus obtain a complete solution to the problem of Gragg and Kung for this class of coprime semidirect products.

title: Inhomogeneous deformations of $\mathfrak{osp}(N|2n)$: triviality for any number of odd parameters
comment: 20 pages. The Lean 4 formalization is available at https://github.com/ritsumei-aoi/osp-odd-deformations
summary: We treat a symmetrized mixed-oscillator deformation family of the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebras $\mathfrak{osp}(N|2n)$, $N,n\geq1$, with even mixed coefficients $β_{u,i}$ and one odd square-zero parameter. We derive the deformed bracket from an oscillator realization, show that its coefficient is determined by the realization, and exhibit an explicit odd primitive, normalized by its vanishing on $\mathfrak{sp}(2n)$. Every odd primitive differs from it by a unique inner derivation. For $N=1$ this is the case $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2n)$ treated earlier. With multiple odd parameters the deformed bracket is the sum of the single-parameter deformations and is again trivial. The trivialization, however, is not additive: it is the product of the single-parameter trivializations followed by a nonsymplectic change of the bosonic generators. The main results are formalized in Lean~4, with the algebras constructed by generators and relations; what is not formalized is stated in the appendix.

title: The Fourier kernel and invariant trace formula of $\rm{GL}(3)$
summary: Trace formula is an important method to study the Langlands program. Arthur obtains the existence of stable trace formula for connected reductive group. In this paper, we will give the explicit invariant trace formula of GL(3). For general reductive groups, Arthur gave an inductive proof of the existence of the invariant trace formula and provided explicit examples for GL(2). For GL(3), we successively compute the invariant distributions, give all the Fourier kernels for the GL(2) cases, and finally obtain the concrete invariant trace formula.

title: Can small transformers learn the language of Coxeter groups?
comment: 13 pages, 13 figures, accepted as a poster at the 6th workshop on Mathematical Reasoning and AI; NeurIPS 2026, Atlanta; This version is updated from the camera-ready version which can be found at https://mathai-2026.github.io/cfp/ and https://openreview.net/forum?id=lYImtIt4tA
summary: The field of mechanistic interpretability is well-suited to collaborative projects between mathematicians and AI researchers. This work describes one such project. We trained a small transformer to learn the language of the Coxeter group affine A2, best known as the symmetries of the tiling of the Euclidean plane by equilateral triangles. We then formulated and proved a word-theoretic conjecture about affine A2 after observing the attention patterns of the trained model.

title: On naturality of cohomological support for small quantum groups
summary: We apply the theory of hypersurface support by Negron and Pevtsova to prove the naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum Borel groups, with respect to restriction to Levi subalgebras. This in turn implies naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum groups for modules that lift to Lusztig's big quantum group, for instance tilting modules. This allows us to make the recent conditional classification of tensor ideals of abelian type in the category of such tilting modules unconditional.

title: Motivic generating functions and $L$-derivatives of cohomological automorphic representations
summary: Forty years ago, Gross and Zagier proved a remarkable formula computing the central derivative of the Rankin--Selberg $L$-function of a cusp form $f$ of weight $2$ and a character of the class group of an imaginary quadratic field, satisfying the so-called Heegner condition, and deduce that the nonvanishing of the central derivative implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding Mordell--Weil rank. This formula was later generalized in various contexts and degrees, for example, by S. Zhang for $f$ of higher even weights; and by Yuan--Zhang--Zhang for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form of parallel weight $2$ over an arbitrary totally real field $F$ and $χ$ a Dirichlet character of an arbitrary CM extension $E/F$, allowing arbitrary ramification. In this article, we prove a Gross--Zagier type formula in the context of doubling method, for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form over $F$ and $χ$ a Hecke character of $E$ of general weights under a balancing condition, again allowing arbitrary ramification. Indeed, we even formulate a general conjecture which we call the motivic arithmetic inner product formula, for cohomological automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_{2r}$ over $E$ of hermitian type of balanced weights.

title: Restrictions to a principal $A_1$-subgroup
summary:
We consider simple simply-connected algebraic groups $G$ over the complex numbers, and a principal $A_1$-subgroup $A \leq G$. We show that for most types of $G$ all its irreducible representations $V(λ)$ ($λ$ a dominant weight) are determined by their restrictions to $A$ up to graph automorphisms.
  The exceptions are groups $G$ of type $A_l$ with $l \geq 5$ and $G$ of type $D_l$ with $l = 4^m$ and $m \geq 2$.

title: On minimal singular vectors of $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ for types $B$ and $C$
summary: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra of type $B$ or $C$ over ${\mathbb C}$. Given $κ\in{\mathbb C}$, let $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ be the universal affine vertex algebra associated with $\mathfrak{g}$ at level $κ$. We characterize the weights of minimal singular vectors of $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ with respect to the generalized Cartan matrix, when $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ is not simple and $κ$ is not critical. Furthermore, we determine the corresponding longest Weyl elements in the Kashiwara-Tanisaki character theorem of the singular vectors.

title: Non-split groups of Lie type and iSchur algebras with unequal parameters
summary: We present a geometric framework for realizing quantum Schur algebras with unequal parameters, via constructible sheaves on flag varieties arising from non-split groups of Lie type. In the special cases of general unitary groups and minus-type orthogonal groups, this framework yields the iSchur algebras with unequal parameters, which are closely related to the quasi-split iquantum groups of type AIII. Such a geometric realization enables the construction of canonical bases, integral forms, and monoidal categorification for these unequal-parameter iSchur algebras and the corresponding iquantum groups. This material is not a formal generalization from the equal-parameter case to the unequal-parameter case. A nontrivial arithmetic structure is imposed on the geometric structure of split groups, giving rise to many new phenomena. For example, the support varieties of generators of an integral form may not be rationally smooth, the categorification is provided by the category of descent data of semisimple complexes fixed by the twisted Frobenius, and the positivity of the canonical basis is established using a refined covering.

title: Webs and exponentially large mu-coefficients
comment: 44 pages, many figures, Lean verification available, comments welcome
summary: Using webs, we prove that Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients for symmetric groups grow at least exponentially with the rank, already for pairs labeled by a three-row rectangle.

title: Irreducibility of Verma modules for symmetrizable Kac-Moody superalgebras
summary: We establish a criterion for the irreducibility of Verma modules over symmetrizable Kac--Moody superalgebras. Our main tool is the Weyl-Kac denominator identity.

title: Homology and higher-order intermediate categories for proper abelian subcategories
comment: Revised the exposition and proofs; updated the abstract, introduction, and examples
summary: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an extension-closed proper abelian subcategory of a triangulated category $\mathcal{C}$, and put $\mathcal{D}_\ell=Σ^\ell\mathcal{A}*\cdots*\mathcal{A}$ for $\ell\geq 1$. Assuming that $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(Σ^p\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})=0$ for $1\leq p\leq\ell+1$, we construct homology functors $H_i:\mathcal{D}_\ell\to\mathcal{A}$ for $0\leq i\leq\ell$ and prove that triangles in $\mathcal{D}_\ell$ induce natural long exact sequences in $\mathcal{A}$. If $\mathcal{C}$ is Krull--Schmidt, we introduce compatible sequences of subcategories of $\mathcal{A}$ and use them to classify the homology-determined subcategories $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathcal{D}_\ell$ that are closed under extensions and direct summands.

title: Mutation of Theta Functions
summary: We give an account of mutation of theta functions in cluster scattering diagrams, starting with a notion of mutation that is related to, but different from, the notion of mutation defined by Gross, Hacking, Keel, and Kontsevich.This different approach to mutation leads to several applications. Three of the applications simplify the process of computing structure constants for multiplication of theta functions, and these are used in another paper on cluster scattering diagrams of affine type. Notable in these three applications is the appearance of mutation symmetries and dominance regions. The other two applications have to do with pointed reduced bases, a variation on the pointed bases of Fan Qin. We give a characterization of pointed reduced bases analogous to Qin's characterization of pointed bases. All of these applications take place in a version of Gross, Hacking, Keel, and Kontsevich's canonical algebra that can be constructed for an arbitrary exchange matrix.

title: The ribbon category of representations of a crossed module
summary: The theory of representations of a crossed module is a direct generalization of the theory of representations of groups. For a finite group G, the Drinfeld quantum double of the group G is a Hopf algebra that represents a special case of crossed module of finite groups. Here we study how to extend the construction of the Drinfeld quantum double for any other kind of crossed module of finite groups. This leads to a Hopf algebra D(G,H) that presents similarities with a Drinfeld double. We then study simple subalgebras of D(G,H) and give two isomorphisms for the decomposition into a product of simple subalgebras. We then study the category D(G,H)-mod^Fd of finite dimensional modules over D(G,H), which turns out to be isomorphic to the category of finite dimensional representations of finite crossed modules of groups. These categories being monoidal, we also study links between direct sums of simple objects and tensor products of simple objects and give some results for a Clebsch-Gordan formula. We, in this context, present and develop the character theory for representations of crossed modules of finite groups, and detail the proofs. We then study the category itself, which leads to some ribbon invariants.
